Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 76 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 34225 of 2022 Applicant :- Munni Bhagtani Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

sentences.text: Counsel for Applicant :- Haya Rizvi,Shamsher Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anurag Yadav,Mahendra Pratap Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the first informant / complainant.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant, who is involved in Case Crime No. 211 of 2021, under Sections 304B, 498A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, police station Ramala, district Baghpat, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, informant, who is father of the deceased, lodged the first information report of this case on 25.11.2021 against Sonu, Jai Kumar, Munni Bhagtani (present applicant) and Bulbul, who are husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law of the deceased, respectively, with the allegation inter alia that marriage of his daughter was solemnized on 15.07.2021 with co-accused Sonu, in which, he had given sufficient dowry as per his capacity but accused persons were not satisfied and there was consistent demand of Rs. 5 lacs from their side.

Munni Bhagtani vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106201022/

sentences.text: Since the deceased was being harassed, she had come to her parental house but on 20.11.2021 at about 05:00 P.M., co-accused Sonu took her to his house and on the next day on 21.11.2021, she was done to death by the accused persons.

It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased,
who was anemic and her hemoglobin was deteriorating and had reached 6.0, which is much below the biological range between 12 to 15.

It is also pointed out that as per the post mortem report, cause of death of the deceased could not be ascertained, therefore, viscera was preserved but till date,
despite repeated time having been granted to learned A.G.A. for the State, he could not produce the viscera report.

It is further submitted that the case of the applicant stands on identical footing to that of co-accused Jai Kumar, who is father-in-law of the deceased and husband of the present applicant, who has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 10.10.2022 in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 23210 of 2022, hence the applicant is also entitled for bail on the ground of parity.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 23210 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant does not have any criminal history to her credit.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.02.2022 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, she will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant reiterating the prosecution case as mentioned in the first information report but they could not dispute the nature of disease and test report of the deceased which has been filed at Annexure No. 7 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that there is no dispute that the deceased was suffering from anemia disease and her hemoglobin was very low as noted above.
The applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and there is no direct and specific role against her.
I also find that co-accused Jai Kumar under similar accusation has been granted bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the accusation, severity of punishment, evidence, complicity of the accused, this Court is of the opinion that the applicant has made out a case for bail on the ground of parity.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Munni Bhagtani, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Munni Bhagtani vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106201022/
2 (iii) That after her release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.

In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail.
